newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Easing US harvest demand dampens diesel diff.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Easing US harvest demand dampens diesel diff.

text.p: Easing harvest demand in the Midwest and last week's build in distillate stocks in the Gulf Coast were expected to dampen differentials on diesel barrels in the cash markets this week, traders said.

"Agricultural demand is winding down," said Laura Anello, an energy broker with FCC-Penterra in Kansas City, Mo., who saw diesel differentials continuing to ease in the Midwest's Chicago and Group Three markets.
Traders also were expected to watch inventory reports closely for a continued build in heating oil stocks.

Total U.S. American Petroleum Institute distillate inventories coming into the week lagged last year's levels by 17.1 million barrels despite a 1.3 million barrel build in last week's petroleum inventory reports.

To avoid entering the winter heating season with the lowest inventories on hand since December 1989, stocks would have to build by an average 1.6 million barrels a week over the next eight weeks, Anello said.
"My feeling is heating oil stocks are still low and we will not rebuild to meet our lowest expectations by the start of the winter," Anello said.

Heating oil differentials in the Gulf and New York Harbor held fairly steady, meanwhile, amid volatile NYMEX movements last week. "That indicates there's not a lot of serious pressure on physical supplies yet," an East Coast trader said.
According to the API, total U.S. gasoline production declined 3.2 percent the week of October 4 from the previous week as refiners maximized distillate output ahead of winter.

"I find very little conviction in the market," one Gulf products trader said, although he echoed market sentiment that gasoline could likely benefit from a reduction of imports from Europe and slackening domestic production.
Although differentials firmed about a half cent Friday on Gulf Coast unleaded M3-grade gasoline, some traders said they thought thin trade rather than a scarcity of barrels had moved numbers higher.

"People might not be showing their barrels," one player suggested, adding many traders were out of the market much of last week at a Conoco golf tournament in Texas and an Ashland Oil outing in Kentucky. In the Midwest, the Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of inventories in the region, reported a 21-day supply of gasoline and 28-day supply of low sulphur diesel on hand, traders said. West Coast trade was still being driven by a 636,000 barrel build in gasoline stocks that left total inventories 2.4 million barrels above year-ago levels. Traders said Chevron contributed heavily to the seasonal build as it stockpiled products ahead of this week's shutdown of its 60,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker at its El Segundo, Calif., refinery. The work is expected to take a month. "I see nothing but flatness next week in gasoline," one Los Angeles broker said. "NYMEX can be as strong as it wants to be and we won't see a reaction." REUTER
